A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReLIFT. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original SFT, RL and ReLIFT experiments, including benchmark results, training dynamics, ablations and a case study.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds evaluations on four OOD benchmarks and a buffer-size/difficulty-threshold ablation.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same GRPO training, hardest-question selection, demonstration buffer and entropy-regularized fine-tuning objectives. Appendix H varies selection thresholds experimentally; the recommended zero-accuracy gate remains unchanged. The asynchronous collection discussion describes feasibility, not an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds actual evaluations on ARC-Challenge, GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Redux and HumanEval. These substantially broaden OOD coverage, particularly through coding and specialized science questions. The existing mathematical training data and six original evaluation benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. Table 5 extends the existing base/instruction models, SFT, RL, RL with SFT loss, both SFT-then-RL variants and LUFFY to new benchmarks; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 3 changes the stated evaluation metric for MATH500 and OlympiadBench from pass@1 to avg@8, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Appendix H introduces a 400-step evaluation on five math benchmarks, crossing four buffer sizes with three difficulty thresholds. Other previously stated protocols are largely retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix H, Table 6 and Figure 9 systematically test sensitivity to buffer size and difficulty threshold through a 12-configuration grid and training curves. This adds substantial evidence about two central design choices beyond the retained scheduling, data-selection and entropy-coefficient ablations.

E5.justification: Section 3 newly specifies eight-sample averaging for MATH500 and OlympiadBench through avg@8, adding sampling/estimation information beyond the earlier pass@1 statement. This does not establish additional independent training runs. Appendix H's 0.49 ± 0.003 summarizes different configurations, not newly reported run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds OOD scores: ReLIFT leads on ARC-Challenge, Redux and HumanEval, while LUFFY leads GPQA, 0.441 versus 0.431. Table 6 and Figure 9 add sensitivity results. Table 1 also revises multiple accuracy entries, including ReLIFT's MATH500/OlympiadBench scores from 87.4/57.8 to 87.9/57.3, retaining 52.6 overall. Given the stated metric revision, these are not established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, difficulty definitions and reward function are retained. The new threshold sweep is an empirical analysis; it adds no substantive theoretical result, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about complementary RL/SFT strengths, interleaved fine-tuning, performance and resource efficiency. The additional experiments support existing generalization claims without redefining their main stated scope.

C2.justification: New Section 6.1 distinguishes the source-agnostic framework from its teacher-distillation experiments, explicitly notes the absence of human-annotation experiments, and argues that asynchronous collection could hide latency under a generation-rate condition. Offline demonstrations were already disclosed in v2. Appendix H additionally attributes poor parameter settings to overly frequent fine-tuning.

D1.justification: Appendix H documents the 400-step sweep, tested Q/M values and recommended configuration. Appendix B corrects the malformed Llama SFT learning rate from '2×−5' to '2×10−5'. Existing implementation details, hardware, chat templates and code-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds four benchmark references: Chen et al. for HumanEval, Clark et al. for ARC, Gema et al. for MMLU-Redux and Rein et al. for GPQA. The dedicated related-work discussion and existing comparisons with prior training approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands Section 6 into Discussion and Conclusion, adds Appendices G–H and acknowledgments, and updates affiliations and publication headers. Most existing prose, including the abstract, introduction and method description, is unchanged; there is no extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v3 adds two tables and a three-panel training-curve figure, clarifies Table 1's ranking-mark caption, and introduces conference headers with some reflow. Existing figures and table structures are retained, so the visual changes are localized additions.

improvement.justification: The new science, knowledge and coding evaluations strengthen generalization evidence beyond v2's single OOD benchmark, while Appendix H tests previously fixed design choices. Section 6.1 also clarifies practical limitations. These gains are limited by sparse protocol details for the new benchmarks and the unexplained retention of old ReLIFT math scores in Table 4 despite the revisions to Table 1.
